title: The Continual Improvement Model

header.html: List the steps of the ITIL Continual Improvement Model; understand each step; describe continual improvement within the ITIL Value System and its role in the organization
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), category 4.6

toc.title: Role in the ITIL Value System

html:
1Why a model

Continual improvement is a recurring activity at all levels, from the whole organization to a single practice. The ITIL Continual Improvement Model gives a repeatable path for each improvement: from vision to evaluated results. It supports the guiding principles (especially progress iteratively with feedback) and is the fifth component of the ITIL Value System.

2The seven steps

Each step asks a question:

# Step Question
1 Vision What is the vision?
2 Current state Where are we now?
3 Target state Where do we want to be?
4 How to get there How do we get there? (the plan)
5 Action Take action
6 Evaluation Did we get there?
7 Momentum How do we keep the momentum going?

[Verify live] The model is described as a refined version of the ITIL 4 model; the seven steps and their order match the ITIL 4 model. Check the official book for exact wording.

Exam tip

. Vision, where are we, where do we want to be, how do we get there, take action, did we get there, keep momentum. The model is a loop: after step 7 the work continues.

3Key points on each step

Step Key idea
Vision Link to the organization's vision and objectives, so improvement serves value
Current state Measure the baseline; start where you are
Target state Set a clear, measurable goal
How to get there Plan small, achievable steps; use iteration
Action Do the work, collaborate, keep it visible
Evaluation Check results against the target; learn from feedback
Momentum Embed the change, celebrate, and choose the next improvement

4Role in the ITIL Value System

Continual improvement touches every other component: it improves the practices, the value chain activities, governance and the application of the principles. It is not a project that ends; it is part of everyday work for everyone.

Exam tip

. The steps are questions you can ask in order: vision, now, target, plan, act, evaluate, keep going. A scenario that checks results against the target is evaluation, not action.

Exam tip

. The model is a loop, not a project plan. An option that says improvement stops after the action step, or happens only once, is wrong.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which is the correct order of the first three steps of the continual improvement model?

  • ACurrent state, vision, target state
  • BTarget state, vision, current state
  • CVision, target state, current state
  • DVision, current state, target state
Show the answer

Answer: D. The order is vision, current state, target state.

S2A team has measured its baseline and now asks where it wants to be. Which step is this?

  • AVision
  • BTarget state
  • CCurrent state
  • DEvaluation
Show the answer

Answer: B. Setting the goal is the target state step.

S3Which statement about the continual improvement model is CORRECT? (1) It has seven steps. (2) It ends once the action step is complete. (3) The evaluation step asks whether the target was reached. (4) Momentum is the first step.

  • A1 and 3
  • B2 and 3
  • C3 and 4
  • D2 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: A. The model has seven steps, and evaluation checks whether the target was reached.

S4Identify the missing word(s). The last step of the continual improvement model asks how to keep the [ ? ] going.

  • AMomentum
  • BBudget
  • CIncident
  • DRelease
Show the answer

Answer: A. The final step is about keeping the momentum going.

S5After a new process went live, the team compared results with the target and gathered feedback. Which step is this?

  • AAction
  • BVision
  • CHow to get there
  • DEvaluation
Show the answer

Answer: D. Checking whether the target was reached is evaluation.

S6Which statement best describes continual improvement in the ITIL Value System?

  • AA one-time project run by the quality team
  • BA recurring activity that applies at all levels and improves every other component
  • CA step that only happens after an incident
  • DA task for the governing body only
Show the answer

Answer: B. Continual improvement is part of everyday work and touches every component.

5.2 Recall questions

R1How many steps are in the continual improvement model?

Show the answer

Seven.

R2What question does the "current state" step ask?

Show the answer

Where are we now?

R3Which step asks "Did we get there?"

Show the answer

Evaluation.

R4What is the last step?

Show the answer

Momentum: how do we keep the momentum going?

R5Which guiding principle does the model support most directly?

Show the answer

Progress iteratively with feedback.

R6Is continual improvement a one-time project?

Show the answer

No; it is a recurring activity at all levels.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Seven steps vision, current state, target state, how to get there, action, evaluation, momentum
Shape a loop; improvement continues
Role fifth component; improves all the others
Old wording the ITIL 4 model has the same seven steps
